observation.visible_scene: A nighttime parade on a paved street lined with spectators on both sides. The dominant object is a large circular float built as concentric rings of LED dots, with a winged fairy figure (green dress, pale wings) mounted near the top of the wheel. A silhouetted person stands/walks in the right-foreground, partly blocking the view of the float.
visible_changes: The wheel rotates continuously: the fairy figure starts upright at the top of the ring and progressively shifts toward the upper-left and then the left side, tilting as it goes, indicating a steady counterclockwise spin of the whole wheel (the spiral light pattern turns with it).
The float's LED color scheme transitions over the clip, beginning as warm white/orange and gradually shifting through pink/magenta to a cooler blue/purple wash by the later frames.
The float grows slightly larger and lower in the frame across the sequence, consistent with it moving toward the camera rather than staying at fixed distance.

The foreground spectator moves from a right-of-center standing position leftward toward the center of the frame and appears to come closer to the camera (silhouette enlarges), while the side crowds remain essentially stationary.
No hard editing cut is visible; the rotation, color shift, and approach appear as continuous physical/lighting changes within one shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the float does before entering or after leaving this segment (whether the rotation or approach starts or stops here).
The cause of the LED color change (operator, music cue, or program) and whether it continues to another color afterward.
The foreground person's intent (filming, watching, crossing) and where they go after the last frame.
The full extent of the parade and whether other floats are in front of or behind this one.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent size increase is purely the float approaching the camera or partly a slow camera push-in/zoom; background parallax is weak, so camera motion cannot be separated confidently from object motion.
Exact rotation direction is inferred from the fairy's leftward drift; the symmetric light rings make the precise angular position hard to read frame-to-frame.
The fairy's pose/leg position changes are part of the wheel rotation, not independent body movement, but the figure is too small to confirm any separate animation.
